name: Rofanplateau
kurzbeschreibung: The Rofan Plateau soaring above Lake Achensee is a high-alpine limestone paradise offering sheer lake drop-offs, the Eagle's Nest viewpoint, and ridge via ferratas.
preis: Free access to trails (Rofan Cable Car charges fares)
oeffnungszeiten: Accessible year-round; cable car operates daily May to early November and in winter
beschreibung:
Überblick

The Rofan Plateau (historically the Sonnwend Mountains) towers dramatically at over 1,800 metres altitude directly above the village of Maurach at the southern shore of emerald Lake Achensee. As the rugged western limestone bastion of the Brandenberg Alps, the high plateau enchants visitors with a striking topography contrasting gentle south-facing alpine meadows with vertical vertical cliffs dropping hundreds of metres to the north. From the rim, spellbinding vistas gaze down into the turquoise waters of Lake Achensee and across to the glaciers of the Zillertal Alps. Atop the 2,039-metre Gschöllkopf summit stands the architectural 'Adlerhorst' (Eagle's Nest) viewing deck—an eight-tonne steel structure crafted like an eagle's aerie that delivers unobstructed 360-degree panoramas over the Karwendel and Tux Alps.

Route & Anforderungen

The Rofan Plateau caters equally to family day-trippers and ambitious mountaineers. The modern Rofan Cable Car whisks passengers from Maurach valley base up to 1,840 metres in just five minutes. From the mountain station, a scenic footpath ascends gently in roughly 45 minutes to the Eagle's Nest platform on the Gschöllkopf. For experienced scramblers, the celebrated Achensee 5-Peaks Via Ferrata traverses five distinct rock massifs (including the Haidachstellwand and Rofanspitze), demanding surefootedness, absolute freedom from vertigo, and full via ferrata safety gear with a helmet. Leisurely trails lead to the rustic Dalfazalm or descend toward turquoise Lake Zirein. Sturdy hiking boots with profiled soles and windproof clothing are recommended across the plateau.

Besuch & Anreise

Travel by car follows motorway A12 (exit Wiesing/Achensee) via federal road B181 uphill to Maurach. Rail travelers alight at Jenbach mainline junction and transfer to regular VVT regional bus services or the vintage steam Achenseebahn, stopping directly at the Rofan Cable Car base terminal. Extensive free parking is provided at the valley lift station for ticket holders.

Tipps

Thrill-seekers can experience the 'Airrofan' skyglider, an exhilarating attraction soaring 200 metres through the air from the Gschöllkopf at speeds of 80 km/h. Savor homemade Kaiserschmarrn on the panoramic sundeck of the historic Erfurter Hütte or Dalfazalm as afternoon light washes over the lake far below.
